title: Adaptive slot governor: simulating microbatch headroom and backpressure under sustained high QPS
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: At sustained high QPS spikes we observe repeated short-lived GPU memory pressure events that cause aggressive KV cache evictions and cascading microbatch thrashing. Existing admission heuristics use fixed thresholds tuned to average load, which either under-utilize GPUs or cause elevated p99 latency and eviction storms.

Goal: Implement an "adaptive slot governor" that continuously tunes microbatch admission thresholds and soft backpressure signals using a combination of short-window EWMA of queue depth, KV hit/evict rates, and a lightweight GPU headroom estimator. We will validate the governor in an offline simulator and a staged canary, instrumenting new telemetry to measure stability and cost impact.

Scope: This ticket covers design, simulator experiments, telemetry/alerting additions, and a staged runtime rollout strategy to test the governor's behavior under synthetic and production-like high-QPS traces. Implementation in runtime will be limited to a feature-flagged path and a default conservative policy for rollout.

Why different from prior tickets: Prior work focused on fixed hysteresis, precomputed thresholds, or token-accounting governors. This approach treats slot allocation as a continuous control problem with smoothing and lookback windows, explicitly modeling KV eviction dynamics and GPU memory reclamation latency to avoid oscillation.
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulator shows >40% reduction in peak eviction rate for representative high-QPS trace without sacrificing >5% throughput
Staging canary maintains p99 latency <= 1.6x baseline during multi-minute sustained spikes and reduces abrupt p50->p99 jumps
No increase in request error rate or silent timeouts in canary (error rate <= baseline + 0.1%)
New telemetry surfaces: per-slot headroom EWMA, governor decision events, KV-evict-rate, and simulated admission score. Dashboards and alerts created.
Feature gated rollout path and rollback procedure documented in Confluence and runbook added to on-call playbook.
design_notes: Core algorithm: compute an admission budget per-GPU slot every 50ms using EWMA(window=10s) of queue length, KV hit ratio, and recent eviction latency; apply a smoothing filter and a minimum dwell time to avoid flip-flopping.
Admission score clamps: [min_slots=1, max_slots=configured_pool_slots]; apply additive increase / multiplicative decrease on transient signals to bias towards availability.

KV-aware backpressure: when eviction rate > threshold, reduce admission budget proactively and trigger KV-prefetch cooldowns; avoid immediate eviction by delaying low-priority microbatches for up to 120ms.
GPU headroom estimator: lightweight sampled resident set + predicted allocation delta from recent batch sizes; not a full allocator change to keep perf overhead <1%.

Trade-offs considered: faster reaction reduces immediate latencies but risks oscillation and increased correctness churn (cache churn); slower smoothing reduces oscillation but may miss quick opportunities to reclaim headroom. Chosen approach favors medium smoothing with explicit dwell-time and simulated preemption windows.
plan: Week 1: Prototype adaptive slot governor in mb-sim-v2 simulator using recorded traces (api/burst_trace_2026-01.csv). Generate sensitivity sweep for EWMA half-life and dwell_time.
Week 2: Implement runtime instrumentation hooks (telemetry events, governor metrics) and a feature-flagged controller path behind 'adaptive_slot_governor' config.
Week 3: Staging canary: enable on 2 nodes in 'staging-1' with synthetic high-QPS load generator; run 6-hour soak with randomized burst profiles; collect telemetry and compare to baseline runs.
Week 4: Review results, address regressions (if any), prepare runbook and dashboard. If green, canary on limited production fraction with on-call present; roll forward via percentage ramp.
Follow-ups: evaluate integration with autoscaler signals and Dedicated pool headroom metrics.
testing_plan: Offline sim: run full factorial of EWMA windows [2s,5s,10s,20s] x dwell_time [50ms,200ms,500ms], collect eviction rate, p99 latency, throughput.
Staging: replay production-like traces and live synthetic bursts; introduce injected KV eviction latencies (50ms/100ms/250ms) to validate robustness.
Canary runbook: automatic rollback on any of: p99 latency > 2x baseline for >5 minutes, eviction rate spike > 2x baseline, request error rate increase > 0.2%.
Unit tests: deterministic simulator test vectors and governor decision logging assertions. Integration tests: end-to-end with small model to verify no memory leaks.
metrics_and_alerts: New metrics: governor.admission_score (gauge), governor.decision_event (counter, labels 'scale_up'/'scale_down'), governor.headroom_ewma_ms (gauge), kv.eviction_rate_per_min (gauge)
Dashboards: Microbatch -> Adaptive governor Overview, show p50/p95/p99 pre/post, eviction heatmap, admission_score timelines.
Alerts: P0 if request_error_rate > baseline + 0.5% sustained 2m; P1 if p99 latency > 1.8x baseline for 10m; P1 if kv.eviction_rate > baseline * 3 for 5m.
SLOs to watch: p99 <= 2s for default models under this pool; also watch 5m rolling GPU memory pressure percentiles.
